name: Monthly Pre-Bill Assembler

parameters.content:
## Monthly Pre-Bill Assembler

### How it works

1. The workflow compiles draft pre-bills monthly, grouping them by responsible attorney.
2. Claude adds a short, dollar-and-age-only priority tip to each attorney's list (never legal commentary — falls back to no tip if the AI call fails, so it never blocks the email).
3. A styled review email is built, logged for audit, and sent to each attorney.
4. A daily process fetches outstanding draft pre-bills, computes each one's own age, and filters to whatever hit a reminder/urgent/overdue threshold today.
5. Reminder/urgent-tier bills route to a styled attorney nudge; overdue-tier bills route to a styled managing-partner escalation instead — grouped by attorney either way, one email per person per run.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio API credentials with the CLIO_BASE_URL variable set appropriately.
- [ ] Configure an Anthropic API key credential for the priority-tip generator (reuse from another deployed template if you have one).
- [ ] Set up SMTP credentials for the emailSend nodes to dispatch emails.
- [ ] Point the executeWorkflow nodes at your Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) via GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID.

### Customization

The code nodes that build email content and group pre-bills can be customized to alter messaging or grouping logic. Scheduling triggers can be adjusted for timing preferences.

## Monthly pre-bill trigger and fetch

Starts monthly compilation by triggering and fetching draft pre-bills from Clio, then grouping by attorney.

## Monthly pre-bill processing and emailing

Processes draft pre-bills if they exist, adds a Claude-generated priority tip, builds a styled review email, logs the workflow, and sends it to each attorney.

## Daily pre-bill nudge trigger and fetch

Triggers daily pre-bill nudge process, fetches outstanding drafts, computes their ages, and filters those due for nudging.

## Nudge handling and splitting

Splits due pre-bills into items for processing and branches based on the urgency tier (overdue or reminder).

## Partner escalation processing

Handles overdue pre-bills grouping by attorney, builds escalation email content, logs escalation, and sends partner emails.

## Attorney nudge processing

Handles reminder-tier pre-bills grouped by attorney, builds nudge email content, logs nudge, and sends reminder emails.

nodes.name: When Monthly Pre-Bill Compilation Runs
nodes.notes:
Fires once a month, on the 25th at 8am (n8n server timezone) by default. Set this to match whenever your firm actually starts its billing cycle — the nudge phase doesn't depend on this date at all, it tracks each bill's own age from whenever it was created in Clio.

This is the only thing that starts a compile run — nothing else in this half of the workflow fires on its own.

nodes.name: Fetch Draft Pre-Bills From Clio
nodes.notes:
Pulls every draft pre-bill in one request. Same bills.json endpoint and 'status' query parameter as the Invoice Reminder Ladder (PAC-18), which already confirmed this works against a live Clio account — 'draft' as the specific status value follows the same convention as PAC-18's 'overdue' but hasn't itself been independently confirmed live, so check your first real run's output matches what you see in Clio's own pre-bill list.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59 — reuse it if already deployed.

Returns up to 200 pre-bills per run. If your firm regularly has more in draft at once, add a loop over the 'page' parameter.

nodes.name: Group Draft Pre-Bills By Attorney
nodes.notes: Bills whose matter has no responsible attorney (or no email on file) are counted in unassigned_count but excluded from attorney_groups — there's nobody to send them to. Check unassigned_count in execution history periodically; a nonzero value means a matter in Clio needs a responsible attorney assigned.

nodes.name: If Draft Pre-Bills Exist
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one attorney has draft pre-bills) → route review emails.
No (nothing in draft — an unusually clean cycle, or nothing billed yet) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip When No Draft Pre-Bills
nodes.notes: No draft pre-bills found this cycle — nothing to route. No emails sent.

nodes.name: Split Draft Pre-Bills By Attorney
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per attorney with draft pre-bills — everything downstream through the send step processes one attorney's review bundle at a time.

nodes.name: Build Priority Insight Prompt
nodes.notes: Prepares the prompt for a short, dollar-and-age-only prioritization tip that gets added to the top of the attorney's review email. Explicitly instructed to never comment on case merits or legal strategy -- this is operational billing triage, not legal judgment (ABA Op. 512).

nodes.name: Generate Priority Insight
nodes.notes:
Calls Claude to generate the priority tip. Errors here (missing credential, rate limit, network) are caught and continue down the error output rather than failing the whole compile run -- 'Extract Priority Insight' treats a failure the same as an empty response and just omits the tip.

Credential: reuse your existing 'Anthropic API key' credential if PAC-31, PAC-50, PAC-60, or PAC-62 is already deployed. Otherwise: Credentials → New → Header Auth → Header Name x-api-key, Header Value your key from console.anthropic.com.

nodes.name: Extract Priority Insight
nodes.notes: Two-layer safety check on the AI tip, same pattern as PAC-60/PAC-62: Claude's own is_operational_safe self-report, then an independent keyword scan for legal-sounding language. Either layer failing -- or the API call itself failing -- just means no tip line, never a blocked email.

nodes.name: Build Pre-Bill Review Email Content
nodes.notes:
Builds one styled review email per attorney listing every draft pre-bill assigned to them, with a Claude-generated priority tip at the top (falls back to no tip if the AI call didn't produce one) and a direct link into Clio's billing view. This is an internal firm email — no client is ever contacted by this workflow.

FIRM_CLIO_BILLING_URL is optional — falls back to a generic Clio drafts URL if unset. The 'automatic reminder' line references FIRM_PREBILL_REMINDER_DAYS so this email and the nudge phase's actual behavior always say the same number.

nodes.name: Log Pre-Bill Routing Workflow
nodes.notes:
Logs the routing event to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33). This is internal record-keeping, not a message to a client — opt-out checking doesn't apply here, same as PAC-18's partner escalation and PAC-59/60's internal notifications.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

nodes.name: Send Pre-Bill Review Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the review bundle to the attorney. Reads all fields explicitly from 'Build Pre-Bill Review Email' rather than $json — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: When Daily Pre-Bill Nudge Runs
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 8am (n8n server timezone). Unlike a shared-deadline design, there's no single 'is today relevant' shortcut here — each bill has its own age, so the fetch runs every day and the filtering happens per bill in the next couple of steps.

nodes.name: Fetch Outstanding Draft Pre-Bills
nodes.notes:
Same query as the compile step's 'Fetch Draft Pre-Bills From Clio', re-run fresh each day. Anything still in draft genuinely hasn't been finalized yet; Clio drops a pre-bill from this list the instant it's reviewed and finalized, so this list is always accurate without this workflow needing to track review state itself.

created_at (used next to compute each bill's age) is included in the fields list but hasn't been independently confirmed against a live Clio response — check your first real run and adjust the field name in both this node and 'Fetch Draft Pre-Bills From Clio' if bills come back without it.

Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the compile step.

nodes.name: Compute Ages And Filter Due Pre-Bills
nodes.notes: The one node to edit for a different review cadence — change REMINDER_DAYS/URGENT_DAYS/ESCALATE_DAYS/ESCALATE_REPEAT_DAYS directly here, or set the matching n8n Variables instead. Two bills for the same attorney can land in this list at different tiers on the same day if they were created on different dates — each bill is judged entirely on its own age.

nodes.name: If Pre-Bills Due For Nudge
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one bill hit a threshold today) → send reminders/escalations.
No (every outstanding bill is younger than the reminder threshold, or none hit an exact match today) → route to Skip. This is the normal, expected result on most days.

nodes.name: Skip When No Pre-Bills Due
nodes.notes: Nothing hit a reminder/urgent/overdue threshold today. Expected for most days — this is the workflow behaving correctly, not a failure to detect anything.

nodes.name: Split Due Pre-Bills Into Items
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per bill that's due for a nudge today — each item still carries its own tier and days_in_draft.

nodes.name: If Pre-Bill Tier Is Overdue
nodes.notes:
Yes (this bill has passed the escalate threshold) → route to the managing partner instead of the attorney.
No ('reminder' or 'urgent' tier) → route to a direct attorney nudge. Each bill is routed individually before grouping, so one attorney can end up with some bills going to them directly and others escalated to the partner in the same run.

nodes.name: Group Overdue Pre-Bills By Attorney
nodes.notes: Run Once for All Items (the default) is required here — this needs to see every overdue bill from this run together to group them correctly, not one at a time.

nodes.name: Build Partner Escalation Email
nodes.notes: Builds the styled escalation email for the managing partner — same 'internal email, bypass client-facing guardrail approval' pattern as PAC-18's 60-day overdue-invoice escalation. FIRM_PARTNER_EMAIL reuses the same n8n Variable PAC-18 already uses, so if that template is deployed this needs no new configuration.

nodes.name: Log Partner Escalation Workflow
nodes.notes: Logs the escalation to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — internal record-keeping only, same as the compile step's logging call.

nodes.name: Send Partner Escalation Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the escalation to the managing partner. Reads all fields explicitly from 'Build Partner Escalation For Laggard' — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json.

Credential: same 'Email account (SMTP)' credential as the compile step.

nodes.name: Group Nudge Pre-Bills By Attorney
nodes.notes: An attorney's bill list here can be a mix of 'reminder' and 'urgent' tier bills — the next step labels the email by whichever tier is more urgent.

nodes.name: Build Attorney Nudge Email Content
nodes.notes: Builds the styled reminder email for attorneys with 'reminder' and/or 'urgent' tier bills — header color and subject escalate based on the most urgent bill present, same idea as PAC-18's day1→day30 tone ladder.

nodes.name: Log Attorney Nudge Workflow
nodes.notes: Logs the nudge to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — internal record-keeping only, same as the compile step's logging call.

nodes.name: Send Attorney Nudge Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the reminder to the attorney directly. Reads all fields explicitly from 'Build Attorney Nudge Email' — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json.

Credential: same 'Email account (SMTP)' credential as the rest of this workflow.

main.node: Compute Ages And Filter Due Pre-Bills

description: Compiles every draft pre-bill in Clio once a month, groups them by responsible attorney, and routes each attorney a single review email with a link straight into Clio. A daily check then tracks how long each individual pre-bill has been sitting in draft — using Clio's own timestamp on the bill, not a shared firm-wide deadline — and nudges the attorney once it's been outstanding a while, escalating straight to the managing partner if it stays outstanding much longer. Replaces the manual chasing that stalls the monthly billing cycle. Logs every routing and every escalation to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — entirely internal, no client is ever contacted.
